A student is chosen at random. (i) Find the probability that the student is a girl. (ii) Find the probability that the student opted for Mathematics, given that the student is a girl. (iii) Find the probability that the student is a girl, given that the student opted for Applied Mathematics.
If P(A) = 7/20, P(B) = 1/5 and P(A ∩ B) = 3/20, find P(A|B) and P(B|A).
items.markingKey: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B); P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A).

items.stem: A blood test is 98% effective in detecting a certain disease when it is present, but it also gives a false positive for 5% of healthy people tested. If 10% of the population has the disease, find the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease.

Reason (R): E(X) = Σ xᵢ P(X = xᵢ).
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
